result.note: Tested the Urea investment policy, India's seafarer and Hormuz figures, and India's diplomatic response to the July 2026 tanker strikes.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 approved by the Union Cabinet in July 2026:
items: It replaces an earlier urea investment framework that expired in 2019.
It offers guaranteed returns of 12% to 16% to draw private capital into gas-based urea plants.
It addresses India's import of about 26% of its urea, mostly from Oman via the Strait of Hormuz.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. The policy also offers rupee conversion of fixed costs after four years, and the Hormuz conflict nearly doubled urea prices, exposing India's import reliance on a politically sensitive farm input.
questions.source: The Cabinet approved the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026, replacing a framework that expired in 2019, offering guaranteed returns of 12% to 16% and rupee conversion of fixed costs after four years to draw private capital into gas-based plants.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, India ordered shipowners and recruiters to stop deploying Indian seafarers on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Consider the following pairs:
items: Indian seafarers supplied to global fleets — more than 300,000
India's rank among suppliers of seafarers to global fleets — third-largest
Share of the world's oil moving through the Strait of Hormuz — roughly a fifth
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three pairs match the story. Because Hormuz traffic is disproportionately crewed by Indians, owners must now find replacements at a premium or idle their ships, giving New Delhi leverage in the Gulf.
questions.source: India supplies more than 300,000 sailors to global fleets, third-largest in the world, and roughly a fifth of the world's oil moves through that strait on vessels disproportionately crewed by Indians.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, missile strikes on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz killed an Indian seafarer, and India summoned Iran's deputy ambassador. Consider the following statements:
items: India's protest explicitly named Iran as responsible for the strikes.
The United Arab Emirates attributed the strikes to Iranian cruise missiles.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because India protested without naming Tehran, while the UAE blamed Iranian cruise missiles. A month earlier India had summoned the US chargé d'affaires over a similar death of Indian crew.
questions.source: The United Arab Emirates blamed Iranian cruise missiles. India protested without naming Tehran.
